observation.visible_scene: A winter woodland under an overcast gray sky: snow blankets the ground and clings to a large mound of cut, leafless branches on the right side of the frame, while bare birch trunks and tall deciduous trees fill the left and background. A fire burns actively inside the branch mound, producing a tall column of orange-yellow flame and faint smoke. At the far right edge a snow-covered open area with stacked logs or a small structure is partly visible.
visible_changes: The flames flicker continuously, varying in height, width and shape from frame to frame as the fire consumes the brush.

The camera gradually retreats / widens its view across the excerpt: the burning pile and its flame shrink relative to the frame, and progressively more of the snowy clearing and the stacked-log/structure area on the right become visible.
The surrounding trees, branches and ground snow remain essentially fixed in position throughout, showing no wind movement or collapse.
Smoke rises weakly above the flame without changing the scene layout.
outside_clip_unknowns: How and when the fire was lit, and what caused the pile to be assembled.
Whether the pile continues to burn down, collapses, or is extinguished after the last frame.
Any unseen person or action that started or tends the fire.
uncertain_details: Whether the apparent shrinkage of the flame is due to camera dolly-back, zoom-out, or both.
Whether any individual branch shifts or falls as it burns, versus mere occlusion by the flickering flame.
The exact identity of the structure/logs at the right edge.
